prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1429; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival in Baytown, Texas, I found a low-speed head-on collision between two passenger vehicles. Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel of the first vehicle and reported pain in the left knee. Driver 2 stated that the vehicles came together nose to nose at low speed, and that account matched what the statements from independent witnesses at the scene described. A Passenger was also in Driver 1's vehicle, and both the Passenger and Driver 1 were seen there by responding units. Damage to both front ends was consistent with the direction and force of impact described, and photographs taken at the scene show no prior body or frame damage on Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 presented an insurance card listing Driver 1 as the named insured on the policy. Driver 1 was transported for evaluation of the knee injury, which I consider consistent with the mechanism of the collision. No citations were issued at the scene.
